title: Should artists speak up about Israel-Gaza?
description:
For the first time in a loooong time, Macklemore’s face is probably all over your timeline, alongside Ed Sheeran’s. This week, Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour’s been plunged into chaos after Macklemore was dropped as Ed's support for making pro-Palestinian comments on stage. The other artists who were going to take part in the tour with Ed pulled out in solidarity. What’s gonna happen with his Philadelphia concert? Is this going to ruin the tour?!

We unpack how the week unfolded with Zara Salaria from BBC News. Do you want your favourite artists to speak about politics on stage? Jordan Kenny from Newsbeat talks us through the different takes. We also discuss what’s next for Ed Sheeran and his career with our human Wikipedia, BBC music correspondent Mark Savage.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討藝人是否應該在舞台上表達政治立場，並聚焦歌手 Macklemore 因在 Ed Sheeran 的巡迴演唱會上發表支持巴勒斯坦的言論而遭剔除所引發的連鎖反應。在 Macklemore 被取消演出後，所有開場嘉賓與合作樂團皆選擇退出演出來表達聲援，而 Ed Sheeran 則發布聲明試圖保持中立。然而，他的公關回應與過往曾為烏克蘭發聲的立場引發部分粉絲質疑。節目邀請 BBC 記者與音樂專家解析各方立場，以及此事件對兩位歌手事業與形象的深遠影響。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores whether artists should address political issues on stage, focusing on the controversy after Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's US tour for making pro-Palestinian statements. Following Macklemore's removal, all remaining supporting acts withdrew in solidarity. Ed Sheeran's statement attempting to remain apolitical sparked backlash from fans who highlighted his past vocal support for Ukraine. The episode features BBC journalists discussing differing fan perspectives and analyzing how the incident has affected both Sheeran's and Macklemore's careers and public standing.
